Notes

The promise to let go keeps colliding with a plea to stay, until permission to leave becomes the only clear gift.

不能再错了

Asked in a June 2025 Interview questionnaire which movie he wished he could soundtrack, Jackzebra chose White Oleander. That supplies a useful connection to his stated tastes for the song’s title. Here the lyric stays with one-sided feeling, inability to speak and permission to leave; the film connection adds a point of entry without turning those lines into a plot summary.

  • Interview: Jackzebra’s own listening and film picks
拿得起我放得下

拿得起、放得下 praises being able to take something on and also put it down: commitment balanced by detachment. In this song the second half proves difficult. “Please don’t give up” follows almost immediately, so the maxim sounds like a posture the speaker is trying to acquire rather than a freedom he already possesses. Its repeated return does not resolve the attachment.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
你说的话我会听

The promise to listen offers cooperation without saying that the other person returns his feelings. In the next section, they do not even know about the attachment. That delayed information changes the opening plea: it may be part of an intimate conversation the speaker can imagine more completely than he can actually have.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
单方面的情

单方面 sounds like “on one side” or “unilateral,” comparatively dry wording beside 情, feeling or attachment. The phrase reduces an emotionally consuming situation to a simple imbalance. It also retroactively changes the repeated “don’t give up”: there may be no shared relationship for the other person to give up on in the first place.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
话说不出来了

The song can sing a plea repeatedly, yet inside its story the speaker cannot say the words. That is a useful distinction between a lyric and an actual conversation: the refrain gives form to what remains unspeakable in the scene. The empty head is not a lack of attachment; it is the point where attachment fails to become speech.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
平淡

平淡 covers the ordinary, calm and unexciting; it need not mean an empty or failed life. Here it is given a 代价, a price: a blank head and words that will not come. That pairing makes uneventfulness costly without declaring that turmoil would be better. The speaker’s “I’m used to it” is then contrasted with somebody younger who may not be.

  • MOE concise dictionary: 平淡
你还年轻

还, “still,” gives youth a time limit, while the next line says the other person will find this difficult to get used to. The speaker briefly assumes the voice of someone who has already endured what they have not. It can sound protective and resigned at once, especially when the promised benefit is permission to leave.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
你可以先走

先 means first or ahead of somebody else. It keeps the image of two people on the same route even while allowing them to separate. Earlier the song asked the other person not to give up; its closing gesture removes blame if they do. That is a real change in what he offers, even if the feeling itself persists.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
